title: The blue-check airline agent
scenario: You post on social media that check-in is broken. Within two minutes, a verified-looking “Airline Help” account DMs you and asks for your booking code plus the one-time code it just sent “to open the reservation securely.”

answers.A: Send the one-time code because it arrived on your own phone, which confirms the airline has your number.
answers.B: Stop the DM and use the airline app, official site, or support handle linked from the airline’s own website.
answers.C: Give the booking code but refuse the one-time code until the account proves it is official.

explanation: One-time codes often authorize account access; support should not need you to hand over a code that proves you are you.
proTip: A code sent to you is usually for you—not for support.
